cls: Topical ophthalmic H1-histamine receptor antagonist / mast cell stabiliser (dual-acting anti-allergic)
pharm: Antagonises H1 histamine receptors and inhibits histamine release from mast cells, reducing the ocular allergic response
tags: Ophthalmic use only - one drop in each eye once daily
For prevention of itching in allergic conjunctivitis
Not for treating contact lens-related irritation
quick: Instill one drop in each eye once daily
Limited data; use only if clearly needed (minimal systemic absorption)
Caution; not known if excreted in milk - systemic exposure is very low
Symptom relief; signs of eye irritation
summary: Alcaftadine is a topical ophthalmic H1 histamine receptor antagonist (with mast cell stabilising and anti-eosinophil activity) indicated for the prevention of itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis. It is administered as one drop in each eye once daily. As a dual-acting anti-allergic agent it both blocks H1 receptors and inhibits the release of histamine from mast cells, and it has been shown to decrease chemotaxis and inhibit eosinophil activation. Systemic absorption from ocular administration is minimal. Contact lenses should be removed before instillation (the preservative benzalkonium chloride may be absorbed by soft lenses), and the product should not be used to treat contact lens-related irritation. Common local effects include eye irritation, burning/stinging on instillation, and eye redness. It is generally very well tolerated.
indications: Prevention of itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis

dosage.d: Instill one drop in each eye once daily
dosage.t: If using more than one topical ophthalmic product, separate each by at least 5 minutes
dosage.n: Approved for patients down to the age studied in labelling

admin: For topical ophthalmic use only - do not inject or swallow
Instill one drop in each eye once daily
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye, eyelids, or any surface (avoid contamination); keep the bottle tightly closed
Remove contact lenses before instillation; lenses may be reinserted after about 10 minutes if the eye is not red
If using other topical eye medicines, administer them at least 5 minutes apart
Do not use to treat contact lens-related irritation
moa: Alcaftadine is an H1 histamine receptor antagonist that prevents the histamine-mediated response of ocular itching in allergic conjunctivitis. It also inhibits the release of histamine from mast cells, and in preclinical studies decreased chemotaxis and inhibited activation of eosinophils. Through these combined antihistaminic, mast cell stabilising, and anti-inflammatory actions on the conjunctival allergic cascade, it reduces the signs and symptoms of the early and, to some extent, late-phase allergic response.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to alcaftadine or any component of the product
relative: Soft contact lens wear at the time of instillation (preservative concern)
monitor: Local eye irritation or worsening redness

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Because systemic exposure after ophthalmic administration is negligible, the risk is expected to be very low; nonetheless use only if clearly needed during pregnancy.
lact: It is not known whether alcaftadine is excreted in human milk after ocular administration. Given the very low systemic exposure, the amount in milk is expected to be minimal; use caution when administered to a breastfeeding woman.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed. Systemic absorption following topical ocular administration is minimal, so renal impairment is not expected to be clinically relevant.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed. Systemic absorption following topical ocular administration is minimal, so hepatic impairment is not expected to be clinically relevant.

major: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions reported (minimal absorption)
moderate: Other topical ophthalmic products - separate instillation by at least 5 minutes
minor: Benzalkonium chloride preservative may be absorbed by soft contact lenses
interactions.diagnostics: No known laboratory or diagnostic interference

monitoring: Resolution or worsening of conjunctival symptoms
counsel: Use one drop in each eye once a day to help prevent allergy-related eye itching
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface, and keep the bottle closed
Take out contact lenses before using the drops; wait about 10 minutes before putting them back, and do not wear lenses if your eye is red
Do not use these drops to treat irritation caused by contact lenses
If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between them
Tell your doctor if irritation worsens or does not improve
pk: Provides protection against itch within minutes; studied for once-daily prophylaxis
Very low plasma concentrations after ocular dosing; systemic Tmax ~15 minutes when detectable
Plasma half-life of alcaftadine ~2 hours (active carboxylic acid metabolite ~4 hours)
Antihistaminic effect maintained over 24 hours, supporting once-daily use
Store at controlled room temperature (about 15-25 degrees C); do not freeze; keep bottle tightly closed
pearls: Dual-acting topical anti-allergic - H1 antagonist plus mast cell stabiliser - dosed once daily, useful as prophylaxis before allergen exposure.
Systemic absorption is negligible, so no renal or hepatic dose adjustment is needed.
Remove soft contact lenses before instillation (benzalkonium chloride can be absorbed by lenses); do not use for lens-related irritation.
Avoid contaminating the dropper tip - a common cause of microbial keratitis with eye drops.
Local burning/stinging and transient redness are the most common effects and are usually mild.
missed: If you forget a dose, instill it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose and resume your once-daily schedule - do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Overdose by the ophthalmic route is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity because absorption is minimal. If excess drops are instilled, flush the eye(s) with lukewarm water. Accidental ingestion of the contents should be managed with supportive care; the small amount of drug and the low oral bioavailability make significant systemic effects improbable.
